crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Deep research agents are software systems that plan and carry out multi-step literature searches, retrieve and read sources, and assemble structured summaries. A landscape scan is a broad, rapid map of a field, covering key papers, methods, datasets, tools, and open questions rather than a narrow systematic review. In evidence synthesis, these agents support scoping, screening, data extraction, and narrative synthesis, while the human reviewer keeps responsibility for judgment. The scope includes both fully automated runs and human-in-the-loop workflows.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These agents run on retrieval stacks, document parsers, vector indexes, and large language models, with orchestration layers that manage search, browsing, and citation tracking. They depend on access to bibliographic databases, publisher APIs, preprint servers, and institutional repositories, plus local storage for PDFs and extracted text. A curated library such as this site's, with 135 research papers and 12,413 extracted claims, is the kind of corpus an agent can query. Compute may be cloud or local, and the agent needs rate-limit handling, caching, and reproducible logs.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical run starts with a research question, then the agent expands queries, searches multiple sources, deduplicates results, and ranks candidates by relevance and quality signals. It reads abstracts and full texts, extracts claims, methods, and limitations, and links each claim back to the original paper rather than to a search tool. The output is often a structured landscape scan with themes, evidence tables, and gaps, which a human then checks against the sources. Iteration and stopping rules matter, because agents can loop or drift without clear criteria.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance is central: every extracted claim should trace to a specific paper, version, and passage, so reviewers can verify it. Rights and licensing matter when agents download, store, or redistribute full texts, and paywalled or restricted content needs appropriate access. Risks include hallucinated citations, overconfident synthesis, missed contrary evidence, and privacy or confidentiality leaks when unpublished manuscripts are processed. Governance covers audit logs, human review, disclosure of AI assistance, and clear limits on what the agent may decide.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Tighter integration is likely between agents and reference managers, systematic review software, and living evidence pipelines. Evaluation will likely focus on recall, precision, reproducibility, and the ability to surface disagreement rather than just summarize. Landscape scans may become continuously updated maps that flag new papers, models, tools, and glossary terms as they appear. The human role shifts toward framing questions, checking provenance, and interpreting findings, while agents handle more of the retrieval and extraction.
